# anyscale_cloud_iam_mapping (Data Source)

Reads the current dataplane IAM mapping of one Anyscale cloud deployment - the ordered rules that route a launching workload to a cloud IAM identity, plus the fallback behavior when no rule matches. See the [`anyscale_cloud_iam_mapping` resource](../resources/cloud_iam_mapping.md) to manage this value instead of only reading it.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_id` (String) The cloud to read the mapping from. To reference a cloud by name instead of by id, look it up with the [`anyscale_cloud` data source](./cloud.md).

### Optional

- `cloud_resource_id` (String) The cloud deployment to read the mapping from. When omitted, resolves to the cloud's primary deployment (`is_default`) and is written back to the data source's result.

### Read-Only

- `fallback_rule` (String) What happens when no rule in `rules` matches: `CLOUD_DEFAULT` or `FAIL`. Null when `rules` is empty.
- `id` (String) `<cloud_id>/<cloud_resource_id>`.
- `mode` (String) The mapping's server-derived mode, currently always `CUSTOMER_MANAGED` once any rule exists. Null when `rules` is empty.
- `rules` (Attributes List) The mapping's rules, in the order they are evaluated - the first matching rule wins. Null when the cloud has no mapping configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Read-Only:

- `selector` (String) The Kubernetes label-selector expression matched against the launching workload.
- `value` (String) The cloud IAM identity this rule assigns when its selector matches.
